=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 86-93 (review_step_timeout input description "Defaults to review_timeout (or 50)" vs default: 50)
  Problem: The input description says the per-step cap "Defaults to review_timeout (or 50)" but the YAML default is the literal 50. Because the input always has a truthy default, the runtime fallback chain at the env level (inputs.review_step_timeout || inputs.review_timeout || inputs.phase_timeout || 50) never evaluates inputs.review_timeout for this input — inputs.review_step_timeout is always 50 when unset. The script-level fallback REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT="${REVIEW_STEP_TIMEOUT:-50}" also defaults to 50. An operator who sets only review_timeout to (say) 90 and expects the per-step cap to follow will get a 50-minute per-step cap while the global timer is 90.
  Why it fails at runtime: Does not fail at runtime — the behavior works. But the description misleads operators about coupled defaulting. The Copilot review comment on this PR (line 93) identified the same mismatch with the same reasoning.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 1693-1704 (JOBS_JSON reuse + JOBS_STEP_JSON fallback) and lines 1764-1771 (per-step guard)
  Problem: When JOBS_JSON is empty (API failure at line 1532) and the subsequent JOBS_STEP_JSON fetch at line 1699 also fails, CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT stays empty and the per-step guard at line 1764 is silently skipped with no diagnostic log. The code falls through to the normal global-inactivity stall detection, which is the correct fail-open behavior, but post-mortem analysis of a stall event cannot distinguish "step budget exhausted" from "API unavailable, guard was never active."
  Why it fails at runtime: Does not cause incorrect behavior — the global timer acts as the fallback. The observability gap matters only during incident diagnosis, when the operator cannot tell whether the per-step guard deferred and then the step timed out, or the guard was never active due to API unavailability.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 1758-1769 (date parsing)
  Problem: The `date -d "${CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT}" +%s` command assumes GNU date. On BSD/macOS runners, the `-d` flag is not supported, so `STEP_STARTED_EPOCH` falls back to 0 and the per-step stall guard is silently skipped.
  Why it fails at runtime: On non-GNU runner environments, healthy long-running review steps would still be marked as stalled because the deferral guard never triggers — the guard condition requires `STEP_STARTED_EPOCH -gt 0`, which fails when the date parsing falls back to 0.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: Lines 1689-1696 and 1752-1760 (API failure handling)
  Problem: When the `/jobs` API call fails, `JOBS_STEP_JSON` becomes empty, `CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT` stays unset, and the stall guard is bypassed with no retry, no fallback to prior cached `JOBS_JSON`, and no diagnostic log.
  Why it fails at runtime: Transient GitHub API failures during a long-running review can cause spurious stall detection on otherwise healthy review runs — the guard silently defers to the old behavior instead of retrying the API call.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR

File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
Line or code reference: Line ~1759 (within the wait-review script block)
Problem: The `date -d "${CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT}" +%s` command assumes GNU date syntax. BSD/macOS date does not support the `-d` flag; it uses `-j -f` instead.
Why it fails at runtime: On BSD/macOS runners (including macOS GitHub Actions runners), `date -d` fails, `STEP_STARTED_EPOCH` becomes 0 (due to `|| echo 0` fallback), and the per-step stall guard is silently bypassed. A healthy long step can still be incorrectly flagged as stalled by the global inactivity timer.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
Line or code reference: Lines ~1693-1699 (the JOBS_STEP_JSON fetch branch)
Problem: When the `/repos/{TEST_REPO}/actions/runs/{RUN_ID}/jobs` API call fails (transient GitHub API error), `JOBS_STEP_JSON` is empty, the `if [ -n "$JOBS_STEP_JSON" ]` branch is skipped, `CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT` stays unset, and the per-step stall guard is bypassed with no retry, no cache fallback, and no diagnostic log.
Why it fails at runtime: A transient GitHub API flakiness during a long review run causes `CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT` to remain empty. When the global inactivity timer later trips, the guard condition `[ -n "${CURRENT_STEP_STARTED_AT:-}" ]` evaluates false, the deferral logic is skipped, and a healthy long-running review is spuriously marked as stalled.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
